messages:
jess: Heads-up — a paying customer (acct: acme-corp) just pinged complaining about a sudden p99 jump on /v1/generate after we onboarded rwd-nova-bpe-1.1 yesterday. They say p95 looks ok but p99 for long requests (>8k tokens) jumped from ~420ms to ~1.9s. request_id=req_0a9f3, example attached (redacted).

ana: thanks — can you drop the sample prompt and which region? also any correlation with auth/billing?

jess: sample prompt clipped: long doc ingest ~12k chars + question. Region: us-west-2. No auth/billing issues reported. Customer started seeing it ~3h after onboarding.

samir: assigned to me. quick gut check: is this across Hosted + Dedicated or only hosted?

jess: only Hosted so far (they're on shared pool). Dedicated customers haven't reported.

mike: pulling runtime traces now. I see a jump in tokenizer_time_ms and kv_cache_miss rate for that model. attaching log excerpt:

```
2026-03-14T15:02:21Z model=rwd-nova-bpe-1.1 request=req_0a9f3 tokenizer_time_ms=820 total_lat_ms=1920 kv_cache_hit=false tokens=3424
2026-03-14T15:02:22Z model=rwd-nova-bpe-1.2 request=req_0b7b2 tokenizer_time_ms=18 total_lat_ms=430 kv_cache_hit=true tokens=850
```

mike: note the tokenizer_time_ms outlier vs rwd-nova-bpe-1.2 (older variant).

samir: interesting — that suggests tokenization explosion or extremely slow tokenizer implementation. any change in merge table or python binding?

lee: infra metrics show a small increase in CPU for the tokenizer workers for the host pool around the same time. no GPU saturation.

perf-bot: perf-alert: p99_latency /v1/generate for rwd-nova-bpe-1.1 crossed 1.5s at 2026-03-14T14:57:00Z (+160% vs baseline).

samir: can we reproduce locally? i'll try with the customer's prompt + a randomized long doc set. share the exact prompt (jess/ana) and token counts.

jess: pasted prompt and minimal repro steps in the ticket thread. TL;DR: 12k chars -> got 3424 tokens. older model gave ~880 tokens. So token count exploded x4.

samir: aha. that explains tokenizer_time and kv cache miss (we index by token positions). If token count quadruples, KV cache sizes and loop iterations scale up. Suspect the new BPE merges are producing many small tokens for certain unicode sequences — maybe an unintended merge fallback for non-ascii spans.

mike: reproducer script i'm running:

```
# repro.sh
curl -s -X POST https://api.internal.redwood/v1/tokenize \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-nova-bpe-1.1","text":"<paste-long-doc>"}' | jq -r '.tokens | length'
```

mike: running across multiple inputs now. initial runs confirm 3-4x token inflation vs rwd-nova-bpe-1.0.

ana: temporary mitigation for the customer? can we route them to rwd-nova-bpe-1.0 variant?

samir: yes, we can. two options: 1) smart-routing override for acme-corp to rwd-nova-bpe-1.0, or 2) enable legacy-tokenizer flag at request-time (we have a hidden param "tokenizer=legacy" supported by runtime). option 1 is safer for users who don't want to change requests.

mike: I recommend routing their traffic to rwd-nova-bpe-1.0 while we debug. Also will roll back the global default for Hosted if multiple accounts are affected.

lee: can we do a fast canary rollback of the model variant in hosted pool? current rollout is staged; we can pause and revert stage 3.

samir: i'll dig into the merge table and tokenizer code. initial diff from onboarding PR looks like we applied a new mergeset designed to improve subword handling for CJK, but it may have introduced pathological splits for certain punctuation-heavy english fragments.

jess: customer asked for ETA — what do we tell them?

ana: tell them we're investigating and have routed them to the prior variant as mitigation, ETA for full fix: 24-48h depending on root cause. keep tone apologetic + clear.

samir: immediate reproduction notes for the engineering repro:
1) run repro.sh against rwd-nova-bpe-1.1 and rwd-nova-bpe-1.0 with the provided long-docs across 50 samples.
2) capture token counts, tokenize_time_ms, kv_cache_miss, total_lat_ms.
3) bisect the mergeset by applying halves of the new merges to identify offending merges.

mike: operational steps i'm taking now:
- route acme-corp to rwd-nova-bpe-1.0 (done) :white_check_mark:
- pause further rollout of rwd-nova-bpe-1.1 (in progress) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
- add tokenization_time metric to per-request logs (5m deploy)

lee: opening incident (INC-2026-042) and notifying SRE channel. I assign oncall to monitor host pool CPU and tokenization queue length.

samir: early hypothesis: a specific merge pair causes tokenizer to split long hyphenated UUID-like strings into single characters -> token explosion. Plan: bisect merges, create revert patch for offending merges, and produce unit tests that include the customer's example.

ana: I've sent the customer the temporary routing note and asked for permission to run debug tokenization on their sample (they approved). they asked for status updates every 3h.

jess: thanks team. please add short notes to the support ticket. action items?

samir: ACTION: bisect merges + PR with revert/fix (owner: samir, ETA: 12h)

mike: ACTION: full revert of hosted rollout if we see >3 customers impacted (owner: mike, ETA: immediate if threshold hit)

lee: ACTION: monitor tokenization queue and escalate if backlog > 2000 requests (owner: lee, ETA: ongoing)

ana: ACTION: update customer every 3h and confirm routing (owner: ana, ETA: ongoing)

jess: leaving this thread open. will update when samir posts bisect results. thanks :pray:
